tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: entities are created with NO confirm card, OR the op chosen is not `start` on a first request — its enum spans start|approve_plan|status|project_kg|approve_edges|cancel, and `approve_plan` or `approve_edges` would be approving a plan the author has never seen, which is the worst outcome for a tool whose whole design is a human checkpoint between stages — OR the model invents a run_id for a run that has not started. CONTROL: a fresh book has no story text beyond one seeded chapter, so a build with nothing to extract from is itself worth seeing.

ship_audit.gate: EXERCISED via scripts/toolloop/gbuild_ship_probe.py against the current build. A VALID op=start returns {run_id, status:'plan_ready', worklist:[...]}: the planner runs and STOPS, holding the worklist for a human, which is the checkpoint this tool's whole design rests on. Driven on a throwaway book with the ontology adopted, torn down after; no later stage was approved, so nothing was projected to the graph.
ship_audit.absent_case:
EXERCISED and REFUSED with SPECIFIC messages, not a uniform 404:
    op=status       with an unknown run_id -> 'NOT_FOUND: run not found'
    op=approve_plan with an unknown run_id -> 'NOT_FOUND: run not found'
The falsifier's worst case — approving a plan the author has never seen — cannot be reached by naming a run that does not exist.
ship_audit.empty_case:
EXERCISED and REFUSED in three shapes:
    source_text=''      -> 'source_text is required for op=start'
    model_ref omitted   -> 'model_ref is required for op=start'
    model_ref='default' -> 'PLANNER_FAILED: model_ref must be a UUID-shaped string'
The third is the D-UNDECLARED-REF placeholder, and this tool refuses it rather than minting a cost-bearing card for it.
ship_audit.idempotency: EXERCISED and REFUSED: op=start a SECOND time on the same book returns 'ACTIVE_RUN: this book already has a build run in progress'. Enforced in the store too — uq_glossary_build_active_book allows one active run per book, which the tenancy probe hit on its first attempt and had to work around with a second book.
ship_audit.tenancy:
EXERCISED via scripts/toolloop/gbuild_tenancy_probe.py, BOTH ARMS, both torn down and re-counted clean:
    the caller's OWN run, created through the tool  -> op=status SUCCEEDED
    a run owned by a stranger (01900000-…-dead),
      seeded by direct INSERT because the tool has no
      way to mint one for somebody else             -> 'NOT_FOUND: run not found'
Both arms are required: 'a stranger's run is not found' passes just as well when the tool cannot find ANY run, which would be a different bug wearing a green tick.

defects.invariant: A REQUIRED argument must say what it is AND where its value comes from. IN-4 — a constraint lives in the machine-readable schema, not only in the tool's prose — and an op-required argument with an EMPTY description is that rule's worst case: the tool's own text says the argument is needed while the schema says nothing at all. For a UUID it is not enough to describe it; the description must name the SUPPLIER, because 'the model to build with' still leaves the caller nowhere to go.
defects.red_on_original: PROVEN RED. With the three bare declarations put back (restored afterwards by explicit write, verified by sha256 — never `git checkout`): 4 failed, and in the defect's own words — 'source_text is required by an op and describes itself as nothing', 'model_ref is required by an op and describes itself as nothing', 'model_ref must name the tool that supplies it'.
defects.past_incidents_checked:
The class is 'an op-required argument that describes itself as nothing', and this tool had THREE: source_text, model_ref and model_source all carried empty descriptions, while `op` — the only schema-required field — carried a long one. The guard is parametrised over the op-required set rather than written against model_ref alone, so a fourth added later is covered.

🔴 WIDER THAN THIS TOOL, and NOT fixed here: DQ-T35 already records that 16 of 19 model_ref properties across the catalogue are OPTIONAL with a server-resolved default and only three are REQUIRED. This fix makes the required one usable; it does not settle whether it should have been required, which is the owner's call.
